title: Bulgogi (marinated beef)
blurb: Thin slices of beef in a sweet soy, pear and garlic marinade, seared fast in a very hot steel pan. Mild.
total: ~1 h, plus 1–2 h freezing and 30 min marinating
intro: Korea's best-known beef dish: thin slices of tender beef marinated in soy, grated pear, garlic and sesame, then seared quickly so the edges caramelise. Pre-sliced bulgogi beef is hard to find, so this recipe shows how to slice it yourself: half-freeze a piece of sirloin or ribeye and it cuts thin and even with an ordinary sharp knife. A steel pan is perfect here: get it very hot and cook in small batches so the meat sears instead of stewing. Leftovers go into bibimbap. For a version with no slicing, see chicken bulgogi. This is a home adaptation built from several Korean sources and has not been kitchen tested.
equipment: Steel frying or sauté pan, 28 cm
ingredients: Beef sirloin or ribeye, in one piece

mise.name: Sliced beef
mise.items: half-frozen beef cut across the grain, 2–3 mm thick

mise.name: Marinade
mise.items: soy · sugar · honey · grated pear · garlic · ginger · mirin · sesame oil · pepper

mise.name: Onion and spring onion
mise.items: onion sliced lengthwise · spring onion in 4 cm lengths

steps.title: Half-freeze and slice the beef
body: Wrap the beef in cling film and freeze for 1–2 hours, until firm on the outside but still possible to cut with a knife.
Find which way the fibres run. Cut across the grain into slices 2–3 mm thick, holding the beef with a claw grip. Cut long slices in half to about 6 cm.
uses: Beef sirloin or ribeye, in one piece

steps.title: Marinate
body: Grate the pear on the fine side of the grater and mince the garlic. Stir in the soy sauce, sugar, honey, ginger, mirin, sesame oil and pepper.
Cut the ends off the onion, halve it and slice it lengthwise. Massage the marinade into the beef with your hands, mix in the onion and leave for 30 minutes, or covered in the fridge overnight.
uses: Beef sirloin or ribeye, in one piece

steps.title: Sear in small batches
body: Heat the empty steel pan on high for about 2 minutes, until a drop of water rolls around as a ball. Add the oil.

Lift a third of the beef out of the marinade and spread it in one layer. Leave it for 1 minute to brown, then toss for another 1 minute until just cooked. Move it to a plate and repeat. A crowded pan fills with liquid and the beef boils instead of searing.
uses: Beef sirloin or ribeye, in one piece

steps.title: Bring it together and serve
body: Return all the beef to the pan with the spring onions and any marinade left in the bowl. Toss for 1 minute, until the sauce turns glossy and coats the meat.
Scatter with sesame seeds. Serve with rice, and lettuce leaves to wrap if you like.

notes: Which beef to buy

Tender, fairly lean cuts work best: sirloin (antrikot), ribeye (kontrfile) or top round. Avoid stewing cuts; they are too tough for quick cooking. Ask the butcher to slice it on the machine at 2–3 mm if they will.
Pear is the tenderiser
Asian pear (nashi) has an enzyme that softens the meat and adds fruitiness. A crisp apple works too. Kiwi is much stronger: use only 1 tbsp and marinate no longer than 1 hour.
Freezing ahead
Marinated bulgogi freezes well flat in a bag for up to 2 months. Thaw it in the fridge overnight and cook as above.

title: Dak bulgogi (soy-glazed chicken thighs)
blurb: Boneless chicken thighs in the same sweet soy and garlic marinade as bulgogi, browned in a steel pan and glazed. No slicing needed.
intro: The chicken version of bulgogi: whole boneless thighs marinated in soy, pear, garlic and ginger, browned in a steel pan, then glazed with the leftover marinade and sliced. It needs no thin slicing, just ordinary thigh fillets. Mild and sweet-savoury. This is a home adaptation built from several Korean sources and has not been kitchen tested.
equipment: Steel frying or sauté pan with lid, 28 cm

mise.name: Marinade
mise.items: soy · sugar · honey · grated pear · garlic · ginger · mirin · sesame oil · pepper

mise.name: Onion and spring onion
mise.items: onion sliced lengthwise · spring onion thinly sliced

steps.title: Open out and marinate the thighs
body: Lay each thigh flat, smooth side down. Where the meat is thicker than about 1.5 cm, make 2–3 shallow cuts so it lies evenly and cooks at the same speed.
Mix the marinade, coat the chicken in it and leave for 30 minutes, or up to a day in the fridge.

steps.title: Brown the chicken
body: Lift the thighs out of the marinade and let the excess drip back; keep the marinade. Heat the oil in the steel pan on medium-high and lay the thighs in, smooth side down.
Leave them for 4 minutes, until deep brown and released from the pan, then turn and cook for 3 minutes. The sugar browns fast; lower the heat if it starts to blacken.

steps.title: Glaze with the marinade
body: Add the onion around the chicken and pour in the saved marinade with 3 tbsp water. Cover and cook on medium for 3 minutes.
Uncover and turn the thighs in the bubbling sauce for 1–2 minutes more, until it is thick and shiny and the chicken is cooked through (no pink at the thickest part).

steps.title: Slice and serve
body: Rest the thighs for 2 minutes, then cut them into 2 cm strips. Spoon the glaze and onion over, and scatter with spring onion and sesame seeds. Serve with rice.

notes: For bibimbap or wraps
Sliced dak bulgogi works in bibimbap instead of beef, or wrapped in lettuce with rice.
A little heat
For a spicy version (dak bulgogi is often made red), stir 1 tbsp gochujang and 1 tsp gochugaru into the marinade.

title: Tteokgalbi (glazed beef patties)
blurb: Patties of minced beef seasoned like galbi, pan-cooked and brushed with a sweet soy glaze. Mild, easy to shop for.
intro: A royal-court dish from Damyang: short-rib meat chopped fine, seasoned like galbi and shaped into flat patties. At home ordinary minced beef with some fat works well. The patties are browned in a steel pan, finished under a lid and brushed with a glossy soy-honey glaze. Mild and good for lunch boxes. This is a home adaptation built from several Korean sources and has not been kitchen tested.
equipment: Steel frying pan with lid, 28 cm

mise.name: Seasoned mince
mise.items: beef mixed with soy, sugar, honey, pear, garlic, spring onion, sesame oil, pepper, starch

steps.title: Knead the seasoned mince
body: Mince the garlic and spring onions finely. Put everything for the patties except the oil into a bowl.
Knead with your hand for 2–3 minutes, until the mixture turns sticky and holds together; this keeps the patties from crumbling.

steps.title: Shape and chill
body: Divide into 6 portions. Toss each between your palms to push out the air, then flatten it into an oval about 1.5 cm thick. Press a shallow dent into the centre with your thumb so it stays flat as it cooks.
Chill the patties for 20 minutes so they firm up.

steps.title: Brown, cover, then glaze
body: Heat the oil in the steel pan on medium. Lay in the patties and cook for 3 minutes without moving them, until browned underneath. Turn, cover and cook for 4 minutes.
Mix the glaze. Uncover, brush or spoon it over the patties, turn them once and cook for 1 minute more, until shiny and sticky.

steps.title: Serve
body: Scatter with chopped pine nuts or sesame seeds. Serve with rice and kimchi, or cold in a lunch box.

notes: Short rib version
For the traditional texture, cut 300 g boneless short rib (kaburga) into small pieces, chop it finely with a knife and mix it with 200 g minced beef.
Grill pan or oven
The patties also work on a grill pan, or in the oven at 220 °C for 12 minutes; brush with glaze for the last 2 minutes.

title: Japchae (stir-fried glass noodles)
blurb: Chewy sweet potato noodles tossed with spinach, mushrooms, carrot, onion and egg in sesame soy. Mild; good warm or at room temperature.
intro: A festive noodle dish: chewy sweet potato glass noodles tossed with separately cooked vegetables and strips of egg, dressed in soy, sugar and plenty of sesame oil. Each vegetable is cooked on its own for a minute or two so it keeps its colour and texture; in a steel pan they go one after another without washing up in between. Beef is optional. This is a home adaptation built from several Korean sources and has not been kitchen tested.
equipment: Steel frying or sauté pan, 28 cm
ingredients: Beef sirloin, half-frozen and cut in thin strips

mise.name: Vegetables
mise.items: carrot in matchsticks · onion sliced lengthwise · mushrooms in strips · spring onion in 5 cm lengths

mise.name: Egg strips
mise.items: thin yolk-and-white omelette cut into strips

mise.name: Sauce
mise.items: soy · sugar · sesame oil · garlic · pepper

steps.title: Blanch the spinach; cut the vegetables
body: Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Dip the spinach in for 30 seconds, lift it out, rinse in cold water and squeeze dry. Season with a pinch of salt and 1 tsp of the sesame oil. Keep the water boiling for the noodles.
Cut the carrot into thin matchsticks, the onion lengthwise, the mushrooms into strips and the spring onions into 5 cm lengths. Mix the sauce.

steps.title: Make the egg strips
body: Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt. Heat the steel pan on medium-low, wipe it with a little oil and pour in the egg, tilting to make a thin sheet. Cook 1–2 minutes until set, without browning, then turn it over for a few seconds.
Roll the sheet up and slice it into thin strips.

steps.title: Stir-fry each vegetable on its own
body: Raise the heat to medium-high. Cook in turn, each with a little oil and a pinch of salt, and tip each onto a big plate: carrot 1 minute, onion and spring onion 1 minute, mushrooms 2 minutes.
If using beef, stir-fry the strips last for 2 minutes with 1 tbsp of the sauce.
uses: Beef sirloin, half-frozen and cut in thin strips

steps.title: Cook the noodles and toss them in the sauce
body: Boil the noodles for 6–7 minutes, until soft and chewy. Drain and rinse briefly. Cut through them twice with scissors so they're easier to eat.
Put them in the hot pan with the rest of the sauce and toss on medium for 2 minutes, until they absorb it and turn glossy brown.

steps.title: Toss everything together
body: Tip the noodles into the big bowl with all the vegetables, spinach and beef, and toss with your hands or tongs until evenly mixed. Taste and add a little more soy or sesame oil.
Pile onto a plate and top with the egg strips and sesame seeds. Serve warm or at room temperature.

notes: Noodles
Use Korean dangmyeon (grey, made from sweet potato starch). Mung bean vermicelli is much softer and will not have the same chew; if that's all you have, soak instead of boiling and toss gently.
Keeps well
Japchae holds for 2 days in the fridge. The noodles firm up when cold: warm them in the pan with a splash of water.

title: Haemul pajeon (seafood and spring onion pancake)
blurb: Long spring onions and seafood bound with a thin, cold batter and fried until crisp at the edges, with a soy dipping sauce.
intro: A rainy-day favourite: whole lengths of spring onion laid side by side, scattered with shrimp and squid and held together with just enough ice-cold batter. Plenty of oil in a well-heated steel pan makes the edges lacy and crisp. Cut into squares and dip in vinegared soy. Mild. This is a home adaptation built from several Korean sources and has not been kitchen tested.

mise.name: Spring onions
mise.items: trimmed to the pan's width; thick white parts split lengthwise

mise.name: Seafood
mise.items: shrimp halved · squid in thin rings

mise.name: Dipping sauce
mise.items: soy · rice vinegar · water · sugar · sesame seeds

steps.title: Prepare spring onions and seafood
body: Cut the spring onions to the width of your pan, about 20 cm. Split the thick white ends lengthwise so they cook as fast as the greens.
Cut the shrimp in half and the squid into thin rings. Pat everything dry. Slice the chilli thinly, if using. Mix the dipping sauce.

steps.title: Mix a cold, thin batter
body: Whisk the flour, starch and salt with the ice-cold water until just smooth; a few lumps are fine. It should be thin, like single cream. Cold batter and little mixing keep the pancake crisp.
Beat the egg separately in a cup; it goes on top later.

steps.title: Lay out the onions and seafood; pour the batter
body: Heat the steel pan on medium-high for 2 minutes, then add 3 tbsp oil and swirl. Lay half the spring onions side by side across the pan.

Scatter half the seafood and chilli over them. Spoon half the batter evenly over everything, just enough to fill the gaps and bind it; you should still see the onions. Drizzle half the beaten egg over the top.

steps.title: Fry, flip, fry again
body: Fry for 3–4 minutes, pressing gently with the spatula, until the underside is golden and the edges are crisp. Shake the pan: it should slide freely.

To flip, slide the pancake onto a large plate, put the pan upside down over it and turn both over together. Add 1 tbsp oil around the edge and fry for 3 minutes, pressing down. Turn once more for 30 seconds to re-crisp the first side.
Make the second pancake the same way.

steps.title: Cut and serve hot
body: Slide onto a board and cut into squares. Serve at once with the dipping sauce.

notes: Korean pancake mix
If you can find buchimgaru (Korean pancake mix), use 130 g of it instead of the flour, starch and salt, with the same water.
Stopping it sticking
A steel pan releases the pancake once a crust forms. Preheat it well, use the full amount of oil and don't try to move the pancake in the first 2 minutes.
Other fillings
Kimchi pancake: replace the seafood with 150 g chopped kimchi plus 2 tbsp of its juice in the batter. Vegetable: courgette and onion in thin strips.

title: Bibimbap (rice with vegetables, beef and egg)
blurb: Warm rice topped with seasoned vegetables, bulgogi and a fried egg, with a crisp rice crust from the steel pan. Mild soy sauce or gochujang.
intro: A bowl of rice crowned with small heaps of seasoned vegetables (namul), beef and a fried egg, mixed together at the table. It's a good way to use leftover bulgogi or dak bulgogi. Every vegetable is cooked in the same steel pan one after another. At the end the pan does what a hot stone bowl (dolsot) does: rice pressed into hot sesame oil forms a crisp golden crust. Gochujang sauce is traditional; a mild soy-sesame sauce is given too. This is a home adaptation built from several Korean sources and has not been kitchen tested.
equipment: Steel frying or sauté pan, 28 cm
ingredients: Soy sauce for the mild sauce
Toasted sesame oil for the mild sauce

mise.name: Carrot, courgette, shiitake
mise.items: carrot and courgette in matchsticks · shiitake sliced

mise.name: Sauce
mise.items: gochujang · sesame oil · sugar · vinegar · sesame seeds — or soy, sesame oil and spring onion

steps.title: Blanch and season spinach and sprouts
body: Boil a saucepan of salted water. Cook the bean sprouts for 4 minutes, then lift them out. Dip the spinach in for 30 seconds, rinse in cold water and squeeze dry.
Season each separately with a pinch of salt, ½ tsp sesame oil and a little minced garlic.

steps.title: Stir-fry carrot, courgette and mushrooms
body: Cut the carrot and courgette into matchsticks and slice the shiitake. Heat a little oil in the steel pan on medium-high.
Cook each one in turn and set them aside in separate heaps: carrot with a pinch of salt for 1 minute, courgette with a pinch of salt for 1 minute, shiitake with the soy sauce for 2 minutes.
Warm the bulgogi in the pan for a minute.

steps.title: Fry the eggs
body: Wipe the pan, add a little oil and fry the eggs on medium for 2–3 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks still runny.

steps.title: Crisp the rice in the pan
body: Wipe the pan again and add 1 tbsp sesame oil. Press the rice into an even layer about 2 cm thick and cook on medium without stirring for 5–6 minutes, until the bottom is golden and crackles.
Lift it out in pieces with a spatula, crust side down, into the two bowls. Or skip this and use soft warm rice.

steps.title: Arrange, top with egg and sauce, mix
body: Arrange the vegetables and bulgogi in separate heaps around the rice, like the spokes of a wheel. Put an egg in the centre.

Mix the gochujang with 1 tsp sesame oil, the sugar, vinegar and sesame seeds, or the soy, sesame oil and spring onion for the mild sauce. Add a spoonful to each bowl and mix everything together at the table.
uses: Soy sauce for the mild sauce
Toasted sesame oil for the mild sauce

notes: Vegetables are flexible

Use 4–5 different vegetables with different colours. Cucumber in thin slices (salted and squeezed), radish or kimchi all work, as do fernbrake (gosari) or bellflower root (doraji) if you find them in an Asian shop.
Without bulgogi
Use 150 g minced beef fried with 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp sugar and garlic, or sliced dak bulgogi, or leave it vegetarian with an extra egg.
